findings.quote: All of them kept the implant once the phage preparation had been given.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE/PARTIALLY. Blind, B is eliminable as an absolute and D ('Their outcomes were compared with those of patients given antibiotics alone') contradicts the stem's own genre marker 'published series', since an uncontrolled case series has no comparator arm; C is an implausible referral narrative. Domain knowledge of phage-therapy case series (majority under control at ~6 months alongside antibiotics) then points to A. The distractors are substantive and the actual figures still need the passage, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick A.

findings.quote: It is confirmed: escape always costs the bacterium something.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. A ('confirmed'/'always') and D ('none of the mutants ... at all') are both eliminable blind as absolutes, halving the field to B vs C with no passage at all. B and C remain genuinely undecided blind, so flag, not kill. Blind pick null.

findings.quote: Interested, but unwilling to let the results so far settle the question.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. On an attitude stem, A (dismissive, 'a distraction from proper antibiotic care') and C ('should already be a standard option') are opposite poles eliminable as overstatements, leaving the single hedged option B against D ('Detached ... without any view of his own'). B carries the canonical key shape for this stem type, so a test-wise reader beats chance blind; D is nevertheless a substantive possibility for expository science writing, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick B.

findings.quote: Att färgen gick ända in till mitten.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE. In vegetable tanning, doneness is judged by cutting the hide and checking that the tan has penetrated to the core, so a reader who knows the craft picks C without the passage. A (fixed time), B (last bath spent) and D (weight) are substantive alternatives a text could plausibly state, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick C.

findings.quote: All efterfrågan på handgarvat läder i köpingen hade upphört.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. B is eliminable blind as an absolute, and D reverses the stem's causality by offering the closure of the calf line as the cause of the shoemakers' switch when the stem asks what caused the calf skins to disappear. That leaves A vs C, which still requires the passage. Blind pick A (weak).

findings.quote: Ungefär var femte bokad timme saknade redovisad verksamhet, mest bland de pass som gått i arv.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. B is eliminable blind ('Samtliga ... minst en bokad timme oanvänd varje vecka' is an absolute) and C is the standard 'the data is unusable' dismissal that does not answer what the comparison showed. D is the only option stating a quantified finding, the expected key shape for this stem, and A is its reversal on the sub-claim about which associations lose hours. This beats chance blind, but the actual proportion still needs the passage. Blind pick D.

findings.quote: Att den inte behövs om tiderna omprövas årligen.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, with within-unit corroboration. C is eliminable blind ('enda sättet'), and q:1's option D ('mest bland de pass som gått i arv') already frames the unit's finding as unused inherited slots, which points to B without reading the passage. A and D remain substantive positions, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick B.

findings.quote: Att seden satte ett tak för gåvan.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, with within-unit corroboration. The Swedish name-day custom is generally known for its token-sized gift, and q:2's option B asserts 'Gåvans tak' as an established fact, so D is pickable without the passage. B (home-made gifts) and C (celebration stayed in the household) are substantive alternatives, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick D.

findings.quote: Namnsdagsfirandet upphörde helt och hållet i samma stund som hushållen slutade slå upp almanackan.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. A is eliminable blind as an absolute ('helt och hållet i samma stund'), and C and D lean on superlatives ('viktigaste råd', 'framför allt') that read as overreach next to B, the only balanced two-clause statement and the canonical key shape for a 'vilket påstående överensstämmer bäst' stem. The lexical asymmetry is visible without domain knowledge, but C and D remain substantively possible readings, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick B.

findings.quote: Detached, reporting the case for and against without any view of his own.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the piece is a third-person signed news feature with no first-person pronoun, and it does quote both a cautious researcher (“They cannot tell us how large that something is”) and a readier clinician (“Josephine Quilvey … is readier than that”), so a student can build a ‘balanced reporting’ case. It is beatable: the writer repeatedly judges in his own voice — “which is worth saying before any of the numbers that follow”, “The clinical record is thin, and honest about being thin”, “the care is warranted: without a comparison group, a recovery in a patient taking four drugs says little about the fifth”, and “that trial, not any series, will decide whether the treatment becomes ordinary”. Those defeat ‘without any view of his own’ and leave B clearly best, so this is an attractive distractor rather than a second key.

findings.quote: That a gang usually turned up to work the ballast within weeks of one appearing.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the passage's own confounding caveat — “Gangs are sent wherever somebody has reported something, Vessholm says, so the quieter miles go uncounted” — gives a real anchor for the reverse-direction reading that tamping follows a reported problem rather than preceding a buckle. It is beatable on the exact prompt (“What are we told about the buckles in Vessholm's log?”): the text states the direction and the proportion verbatim — “his log runs to 39 buckles … and two in three came in the eight weeks after ballast work” — while A adds the unstated quantifiers ‘usually’ and ‘within weeks of one appearing’, and “something” reported is never identified as a buckle. Key B remains clearly best; flagging because the distractor is strong enough that adjudication should see the case.

findings.quote: tomten blev upplag för vägkassens grus
findings.note: class 1 (wrong derivation/inflection): the intended sense is the road-maintenance fund, i.e. 'kassa' (en kassa, definite 'kassan', genitive 'kassans'). 'vägkassens' presupposes a base noun *'vägkasse' (kasse = carrier bag/net), which yields 'the road bag's gravel'. Swedish -a feminines never take -en in edited prose (cf. sjukkassan, arbetslöshetskassan, Försäkringskassan); the authentic HP corpus shows only -kassan/-kassans for fund words and -kassen only for 'plastkassen'. Native alternative: 'upplag för vägkassans grus'.

findings.quote: ber om en timme i en gymnastiksal en tisdagkväll
findings.note: class 1 (compound joint / missing foge-s): edited sakprosa writes “tisdagskväll” with the linking -s (måndagskväll, fredagskväll); the s-less compound belongs to colloquial or transcribed speech. The unit contradicts itself — the title reads “Tisdagskvällar i Vässlinges gymnastiksalar” with the -s. Not lethal because the s-less form does occur in informal native writing (one instance of “fredagkväll” in the authentic HP corpus, inside colloquial first-person narration), but a copy editor of this register fixes it. Native alternative: “en tisdagskväll”.

findings.quote: tomten blev upplag för vägkassens grus
findings.note: class 1/4: wrong declension of an existing word (the *slipen* class). The base noun is 'vägkassa' (the road district's treasury); 'kassa' is a first-declension en-noun with definite 'kassan' and definite genitive 'kassans'. 'vägkassens' back-forms a non-existent base 'vägkasse' (only 'kasse' = carrier bag inflects that way). Native alternative: 'upplag för vägkassans grus'.

findings.quote: ber om en timme i en gymnastiksal en tisdagkväll
findings.note: class 1: missing foge-s in a weekday compound. Norm form is 'tisdagskväll' (cf. måndagsmorgon, fredagskväll); as a single compound noun 'en tisdagkväll' is a compounding error that does not survive edited sakprosa. The unit's own title spells it correctly ('Tisdagskvällar i Vässlinges gymnastiksalar'), which proves this is an error and not a stylistic choice. Native alternative: 'en tisdagskväll'.

findings.quote: det ändrar hur mitt förslag måste se ut
findings.note: class 6: idiomatic temperature. 'ändra hur X måste se ut' mirrors English 'changes what my proposal has to look like'; edited Swedish would more naturally use 'och det påverkar hur mitt förslag måste se ut' or simply 'och det ändrar mitt förslag'.

findings.quote: Att en påbörjad garvning inte gick att flytta med sig.
findings.note: class 6: 'flytta med sig' is not an established particle construction in edited sakprosa; it reads as a colloquial/house-move phrase pasted onto an abstract process. A native writer would write 'inte gick att flytta' or 'inte gick att ta med sig'.

findings.quote: Det hängdes upp på torkvinden och blev liggande tills en beställning kom
findings.note: class 6: collocation clash - the leather is first hung up ('hängdes upp') and then said to 'bli liggande'. Native: 'blev hängande' (or drop 'hängdes upp').

findings.quote: kylan bromsade och en varm sommar skyndade på
findings.note: class 6: 'skynda på' used absolutely with an inanimate subject is off; native sakprosa would use 'påskyndade (garvningen)' or 'en varm sommar skyndade på förloppet'.

findings.quote: blev liggande tills en beställning kom, någon gång ett halvår
findings.note: class 6: the elliptic 'någon gång ett halvår' is clipped; native: 'ibland ett halvår' / 'någon gång upp till ett halvår'.

findings.quote: ber om en timme i en gymnastiksal en tisdagkväll
findings.note: class 1: wrong compound joint - the weekday+time compound requires the foge-s ('tisdagskväll', SAOL); 'tisdagkväll' as one word is a non-form. The unit's own title writes 'Tisdagskvällar', so the passage contradicts itself. A native copy editor catches this instantly. Native: 'en tisdagskväll' (or two words, 'på tisdag kväll').

findings.quote: Hon har rätt i båda delarna, och det ändrar hur mitt förslag måste se ut.
findings.note: class 2/6: 'ändrar hur ... måste se ut' mirrors English 'changes how my proposal must look'; native sakprosa: 'det påverkar hur mitt förslag måste utformas'.
